name: Stacking-chain probe: does stereo z-recovery degrade with stack depth?
question: P275 showed a single off-plane probe needs two views. Does the stereo z-recovery survive a CHAIN of stacked objects (depth built on depth), and does the single-view plane prior fail exactly as predicted (error = accumulated stack height)?

environment.reuse: P275 renderer + geometry module unchanged (same two-view stereo rig, baseline 15 cm)
environment.scenes: 12 synthetic tabletop scenes; free palette colors determine chain depth: 4 table objects -> 2 layers stacked on the tallest host, 5 -> 1 layer, 6 -> none. Chain depth 0/1/2 across 4 scenes each.
environment.measurement: scene-graph reconstruction only, zero LLM calls; two-view vs single-view (table-plane prior)

predictions.claim: Two-view z-error median < 2 cm for every chain layer, at depth 1 and depth 2 alike (no meaningful degradation with depth).
predictions.falsifies: If z-error grows clearly with depth (layer2 >> layer1), triangulated z does not transfer through the chain and the spatial language needs explicit support for hierarchical depth.

predictions.claim: Single view + plane prior: z-error of layer k equals its true height above the table (collapsed to 0 by construction), and xy-error grows with chain depth (the off-plane centroid shifts the projected ray outward); two-view xy stays flat across depths.
predictions.falsifies: If single-view xy does not degrade with depth, the plane prior is stronger than claimed; if two-view xy degrades, stereo has its own depth-transfer problem.

predictions.claim: Two-view xy error on chain layers stays < 2 cm median at all depths (stereo does not lose lateral accuracy off-plane).

fairness_notes: Same rig, same segmentation, same triangulation as P275 (no tuning between experiments).
Chain layers are smaller than their host (physically stackable, each layer's side visible from both views).
Zero LLM involvement: this probes the geometry module only.
